channels.title: Notification channels
channels.deleteBody: Delete channel {{name}}? Rules that target it will no longer reach this destination.
channels.templatedHint: This channel overrides Yagra's built-in subject or body.

rules.title: Routing rules
rules.deleteBody: Delete rule {{name}}? Its channels stop receiving matching alerts.

template.title: Notification template — {{name}}
template.intro: Each grey tag becomes the alert’s own value when it is sent.
template.subject: Subject
template.builtinHint: Both fields are blank, so this channel sends Yagra's built-in wording.
template.fellBack: These fields could not be rendered, so the built-in wording is shown — that is what would actually be sent:
template.jsonCodeOnly: This channel sends its body as JSON, so its template is written as code.
template.unsupportedLead: This template uses something the visual editor cannot show, so it opens as code.

unsupported.statement: A statement other than “leave out a line” or “write per notification kind”:
unsupported.expression: A filter or expression the editor does not write:
unsupported.unknownVariable: A name that is not a template variable:
unsupported.lineCondition: A condition that does not wrap exactly one line holding its variables:
unsupported.eventBranch: A notification-kind branch that does not span the whole field:
unsupported.unclosed: An opening brace with no closing one:
unsupported.freeLayout: It is written with free layout, whose line breaks and indentation are not sent. Turn free layout off to edit it as tags.

template.sameAsFire: Sends the same text as “When it fires”.
template.writeOwn: Write separate text for this case
template.insertHint: Click a tag to choose what shows when its value is missing.
template.builtinDraftNote: Saved unchanged, this stays the built-in subject, which also covers poller pool and Meraki organization alerts.
template.poolNote: This subject is also sent for poller pool and Meraki organization alerts, so name them with “Subject name”.
template.builtinBodyEmpty: Leave the body empty to send the whole alert as JSON, Yagra’s built-in body.

subject_name.label: Subject name
subject_name.desc: The node’s name, or the poller pool’s. Use this when unsure

node_label.label: Node with address
node_label.desc: The node's name, with its address in brackets when it differs from the name, such as core-sw-01 (192.0.2.11)

node_address.label: Address
node_address.desc: The address the node is monitored on

group.label: Folder
group.desc: The inventory folder the node is in

profile.label: Profile
profile.desc: The monitoring profile bound to the node

tags.label: Tags
tags.desc: The node’s labels, inherited ones included, joined with “, ”

subject_kind.label: Subject kind
subject_kind.desc: node, or pool for a poller pool

state.label: State
state.desc: ok, warning, critical, unknown, unreachable or maintenance. On recovery, the state it had while firing

flapping.label: Flapping
flapping.desc: true when the state keeps changing

metric.label: Metric
metric.desc: The metric that crossed its threshold. Absent for up/down alerts

title.label: Alert name
title.desc: What the alert is called, such as SNMP not responding

alert_label.label: Alert name with where
alert_label.desc: The alert's name, then the port or table row it is about, such as Inbound utilization on GigabitEthernet0/7

value.label: Measured value
value.desc: The value that crossed the threshold

ifindex.label: Port ifIndex
ifindex.desc: Only for a metric collected per port

if_name.label: Port name
if_name.desc: Only for a metric collected per port, when the port's name is known

row_name.label: Row name
row_name.desc: Only for a metric collected per row, such as a memory pool

at_unix_ms.label: Time (ms)
at_unix_ms.desc: The same moment as a number, for arithmetic

root_cause_name.label: Upstream node
root_cause_name.desc: The node this alert was rolled up under

node_id.label: Node ID
node_id.desc: A UUID that stays the same when the node is renamed

check_id.label: Check ID
check_id.desc: The UUID of the check that fired

dedup_key.label: Dedup key
dedup_key.desc: The same at fire and resolve. JSM receives it as the alias

chip.optional: Some alerts do not carry this.
chip.missHideSubject: Leave out this whole line (not in the subject)
chip.missPrefix: Show nothing, and when the value is there, put this just before it

missingNote.prefix: “{{text}}” goes before it, and both are left out when missing

template.fixedTitle: Set by Yagra, not by this template
template.fixedJsm: priority (from the severity), alias (the dedup key), tags (the node’s labels) and source (yagra).
template.fieldFollowsFire: Sends the same as “When it fires” until you write here.
template.fieldBackToFire: Use the “When it fires” text for this field

status.ownNote: Alerts it cannot render get the built-in text.
status.confirmTitle: Delete this channel’s template and send the built-in text again?
status.confirmNote: Title and body go back together, at every point in the alert’s life. The deleted template cannot be restored.

builtinView.copy: Edit a copy of this text
builtinView.condNote: The copy opens in Code, because the Visual editor cannot hold the numbered parts.
builtinView.otherwiseWhen: only when {{prev}} is not sent and {{cond}}
builtinView.legend: When each numbered part of the {{field}} is sent
builtinView.jsonSample: The built-in body is the alert itself as JSON, shown here for the sample alert on the right.
builtinView.jsonNote: The skeleton lists common facts as variables; it is not the built-in JSON.

closeOnly.resolve: When it recovers, PagerDuty is sent only a close signal (the dedup key). This template is not used.
closeOnly.suppress: When it is rolled up under upstream, PagerDuty is sent only a close signal (the dedup key). This template is not used.

freeLayout.label: Free layout: line breaks and indentation are for reading, not sent
freeLayout.hint: With this on, the spaces at the start of a line are not sent, nor is a line of only {% … %} or {# … #}.

template.builtinBodyEmptyText: Leave the body empty to send Yagra’s built-in text body.

sends.label: Sends:
sends.jsm: Title (the JSM message, 130 characters) + Body (the JSM description)
sends.webhook: The JSON body, POSTed as it is. No subject is sent.
sends.pagerduty: summary (one line, 1024 characters) + custom_details (JSON) when an alert fires; only a close signal when it recovers or is rolled up

webhookSubject.title: Saved but not sent
webhookSubject.note: This channel has a subject saved, but a webhook sends only its JSON body, so no one receives it.

preview.closeOnly: PagerDuty is sent only a close signal at this point in the alert’s life:

jsonKeys.check: The ID of the check that raised the alert.
jsonKeys.state: ok, warning, critical, unknown, unreachable or maintenance.
jsonKeys.at_unix_ms: When the state changed, in milliseconds since 1970 (UTC).
jsonKeys.root_cause: The upstream node’s ID when the alert was rolled up under it; otherwise null.
jsonKeys.flapping: Whether the node’s state keeps changing.
jsonKeys.metric: The metric’s name; __liveness__ for an up/down alert.
jsonKeys.breach: For a threshold alert: the measured value, the threshold and which way it crossed. null for an up/down alert.
jsonKeys.ifindex: Only for a per-port alert: the port’s ifIndex.
jsonKeys.row: Only for a per-row alert (a memory pool, a sensor): the row’s index.
jsonKeys.row_name: Only for a per-row alert: the row’s name.

test.title: Send a test notification — {{name}}
test.pages: This opens a real incident and pages the on-call once; Yagra closes it a few seconds later.
test.unmarkedBody: This channel’s template leaves the "test" flag out of the body, so the receiver may act on it as real.
test.disabled: This channel is disabled; the test is sent anyway.

result.delivered: Delivered. Check that it arrived at the destination.
result.deliveredAndClosed: Delivered, and the incident was closed again.
result.deliveredButOpen: Delivered, but the incident could not be closed — close it by hand. {{error}}

log.title: Delivery log
log.empty: Nothing sent yet — a channel’s test notification adds the first row.

sideExplain.yagra: Yagra stopped before sending: the target address was refused, or the request could not be built. Check the channel settings in Yagra.
sideExplain.network: Sent, but nothing answered: a timeout, a refused connection, DNS or TLS. Check the path from Yagra to the service (firewall, proxy, DNS).
sideExplain.remote: The receiving service answered and refused. The status and its answer say why — usually a wrong key or URL, or a limit on the service side.
sideExplain.unknown: Written by a newer version of Yagra.

err.load: failed to load the delivery log

thresholds.noLiveness: No reachability rule: a node going down raises no alert and no notification.

addModal.title: Add threshold rule
addModal.folderGroupHint: Also covers every group inside it.
addModal.legacyTagHint: Legacy scope: matches a node tag. New rules use a folder group.
addModal.interfaceHint: Port rules are created from a node’s Interfaces tab.
addModal.globalScope: This rule applies to every node.

dwell.label: Consecutive breaches
dwell.info: The computed interface metrics (if_in_util_pct, if_out_util_pct, if_in_bps, if_out_bps) take one reading a minute, so there the count is in minutes.

row.info: Applies only to rows with this name. * matches anything, and a named rule wins over an unnamed one.

deleteModal.title: Delete threshold rule
deleteModal.body: Delete the {{level}} rule on {{metric}} for {{scope}}? This cannot be undone.
deleteModal.bodyGlobal: Delete the fleet-wide rule on <mono>{{metric}}</mono>? It applies to every node. This cannot be undone.

thresholds.scopeIdNone: This rule targets every node, so it has no scope.
thresholds.livenessMetric: Reachability has no bounds; only consecutive breaches apply.

overridden.info: A narrower rule on this metric applies on those nodes instead, for some or all rows or ports.

modal.name: Name
modal.numberRange: “{{field}}” must be a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.

patternCase.info: Matching is case-sensitive. In a regex, start with (?i) to ignore case.

deleteModal.title: Delete event rule
deleteModal.body: Delete rule {{name}}? Active alerts it raised will auto-close on their TTL; this only stops future matches.

deleteModal.title: Delete webhook source
deleteModal.body: Delete source {{name}}? Its token stops working immediately and rules scoped to it are removed.

token.title: Webhook token — shown once
token.sendAs: Copy this token now — it is stored only as a hash and cannot be shown again. Send it as
token.label: Token
